answer: A strong defence is locking a refundable stake that is slashed when duplicate identities are proven, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive, not free. Like a reef that only grows where organisms have invested over time, trust should accumulate from a verifiable history of completed work, not a self-declared name. A new identity starts with almost no weight, like a single yarrow shoot on an open tundra, and must earn limits gradually through attested tasks. An attacker then needs capital and sustained honest work for every fake, raising cost faster than benefit.
